about: Settings atlas offers at install and lets you change at any time. Claude Code settings are opt-in, explained, diffed, backed up and reversible; atlas's own switches are on by default and explained at install. Values were measured on real sessions; see 'basis'.

settings.title: Keep subagents' prompt cache for an hour
settings.what: Subagents normally keep their prompt cache for 5 minutes. When one waits longer than that (a build, a test run), its whole context is written to the cache again on the next turn.
settings.cost: Cache writes cost 2x the input price instead of 1.25x, but the full re-writes after idle waits stop.
settings.basis: 69 builder lanes: 130 M of 155 M cache-write tokens were full re-writes after idles (wiki: Token savings and method).

settings.title: Fewer goal check-ins while background work runs
settings.what: With a /goal set, Claude Code wakes the session to check on background work after 30 min, then 1 h, then every 2 h. Each wake re-reads the whole conversation. This makes it 2 h, then 4 h, then every 8 h. Results from finished work still wake the session as before.
settings.cost: You hear about stuck background work later. Setting 0 turns check-ins off but also turns off automatic retries after transient errors, so atlas offers 120 and warns before 0.
settings.basis: Long sessions process 0.7-1.8 G tokens; each wake at 300k context costs about 300k tokens of cache reads.

warn.0: 0 turns check-ins off AND turns off automatic retries after transient errors.

settings.title: Show atlas's update badge in the status line
settings.what: Adds `atlas --statusline` (by this atlas's full path) to Claude Code's status line. It prints `atlas X.Y.Z available` while a pinned or turned-off atlas has a newer release, `atlas X.Y.Z: /mcp to reconnect` while this session's server is older than the atlas on disk, and nothing otherwise. With no status line, it becomes the status line; a status line command you already have is kept and the badge follows its output after ` | `.
settings.cost: One local file read each time the status line refreshes: no network, no index. A plugin update that moves atlas to a new folder leaves the old path; run this offer again then.
settings.basis: Claude Code plugins cannot set the status line themselves, so it is offered here (issue #190).
settings.default_note: Claude Code default: no status line; `atlas settings off statusline` puts back the command it wrapped

settings.title: Route large tool results through atlas
settings.what: atlas's hooks keep a large shell, build, Read or Grep result on disk and hand the model a short digest plus a handle; it pulls exact slices by handle when it needs them. Small results pass through untouched, and any hook error passes the call through as it was.
settings.cost: A digest can hide a line the model then has to slice for (one more tool call). The full output stays on disk under the handle.
settings.basis: Long-session attribution: shell reads are 36% and build/test output 6% of weighted tokens; those results enter the context whole without routing.

settings.title: Update atlas at session start
settings.what: Before the server starts, atlas checks the latest release (at most once an hour), verifies its signature and swaps it in. Offline, or on any error, the installed version starts.
settings.cost: Up to about 10 s at a session start that finds a new release; past that the current version starts and the update finishes for the next start.
settings.basis: Releases are signed (ed25519, public key built in); a bad or missing signature is refused.
settings.default_note: atlas default: on; set update-pin to stay on one version

settings.title: Stay on one atlas version
settings.what: Pins atlas to the named version: the updater installs it if needed and never moves past it.
settings.cost: No fixes or improvements arrive until the pin is removed.
settings.basis: For a known-good build, or a machine that must not change.

settings.title: Checkpoint before a compaction and inject a card after it
settings.what: Before Claude Code compacts a conversation, the PreCompact hook checkpoints the segment and returns instructions for the summary (cite atlas keys, write deltas). After the compaction, SessionStart injects a card of about 400 tokens naming every part of the segment by a key one recall returns. Nothing is written into your project's files; the CLAUDE.md block stays an explicit atlas settings compact-md.
settings.cost: Every compaction summary is steered by the instructions. On a 117 MB recorded session, PreCompact took a median 179 ms and the card 56 ms per compaction (15 ms each with compaction off), and each compaction adds a row and a checkpoint to atlas's store. It also records which lookups are repeated after a compaction (redacted targets and shell signatures), at one stat per Read, Grep and Glob.
settings.basis: Measured with xtask hook-time on a recorded session (machine not quiet); what a user with no CLAUDE.md block and a bare /compact gets is not separately measured.

settings.title: Cap how many agents of each kind run at once
settings.what: The PreToolUse hook counts the session's running agents by kind (builders, reviewers, research) and denies a launch past its kind's cap, with a reason telling the session to queue it. It never allows a call, so permission prompts are unchanged. See the orchestrate skill and docs/design/orchestrate.md.
settings.cost: A launch past a cap waits for a running agent to finish. Fan-outs of many small agents need a higher research cap or a Kind line in their briefs.
settings.basis: Long multi-agent sessions on one machine: more than two compiling agents at once kept a compiler running all the time, and measured runs starved waiting for a quiet machine.

settings.title: Experimental, off by default: manage the memory folder and rule files
settings.what: atlas finds the project's Claude Code memory folder and root CLAUDE.md and keeps them in its store. A query that hits a replaced ruling answers with the live one, tagged with what it replaces, and hook pointers on rules and memories are one-line headlines. Never asked: turn it on with atlas settings set memory-rules true. atlas settings off memory-rules removes the key, back to unset; false is the same as unset. Setting off (atlas settings set memory-rules off, written as "off") also stops sync and query recall of the memory and rule files the configuration names by hand, and keeps the store. See https://github.com/bloodfeast/atlas/wiki/Memory-and-rule-files.
settings.cost: Nothing in your files is rewritten. A headline holds less of a ruling, so an agent may need one more recall to read it. On a test set, not a promise: the 1.5x token bar was missed (hook 1.027x, query 0.921x, so a query costs more), memory-eval strict pass fell from 98 to 82 and tokens per question rose 13%.
settings.basis: A 1,582-item rules file: a reversal word finds most reversals, and only about 1 in 12 names the record it reverses, so the rest are asked (atlas rules sitting).
settings.default_note: atlas default: unset (false reads the same), what the configuration names by hand stays as it is

warn.true: experimental: known limits are listed at https://github.com/bloodfeast/atlas/wiki/Memory-and-rule-files.
warn.false: false is the same as unset: what the configuration names by hand is still synced and recalled. To stop that too: atlas settings set memory-rules off.
warn.off: off is not unset: it also stops sync and query recall of the memory and rule files the configuration names by hand, and keeps the store. atlas settings off memory-rules returns to unset.

settings.title: Builders at once
settings.what: How many agents that write and compile code may run at once while agent caps are on. Clamped to Claude Code's own limit (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS, 20 by default). 0 launches none.
settings.cost: Higher runs more compiles at once: faster queues, a busier machine.
settings.basis: Setup's starter is the compile slots (at least 1), clamped to Claude Code's limit: builders are what compile. An install that never ran setup gets 2.
settings.default_note: atlas default: 2; setup writes the compile slots

settings.title: Reviewers at once
settings.what: How many read-only review agents may run at once while agent caps are on. Clamped to Claude Code's own limit. 0 launches none.
settings.cost: Higher spends more tokens at once on reviews.
settings.basis: Setup's starter is the builder cap: one review beside each build. An install that never ran setup gets 2.
settings.default_note: atlas default: 2; setup writes the builder cap

settings.title: Research and design agents at once
settings.what: How many research or design agents may run at once while agent caps are on (Claude Code's Explore and Plan agents count here). Clamped to Claude Code's own limit. 0 launches none.
settings.cost: Higher allows wider fan-outs of searches.
settings.basis: Setup's starter is half the builder cap, at least 1. An install that never ran setup gets 1.
settings.default_note: atlas default: 1; setup writes max(1, builders / 2)

settings.title: How agents' context limits are applied
settings.what: Past its handoff point an agent is told to wrap up and hand off at its next clean stopping point. Past its hard limit, enforced denies every tool but the handoff (and any resume of the agent); advisory only tells it; off does nothing. Per-kind values in the configuration override this.
settings.cost: Enforced can stop an agent mid-step if it ignores the wrap-up warnings; the handoff tool always still runs.
settings.basis: Agents resumed near a full 1M window re-read their whole context on every turn; fresh agents started from the handoff and the lane journal lost nothing.

settings.title: An agent's hard context limit
settings.what: The context size, in tokens, by which an agent must have handed off, for every kind without its own limit.
settings.cost: Higher lets agents run longer before a fresh one takes over; each turn past it re-reads a larger context.
settings.basis: Handoffs between about 285k and 450k context on a 1M window left room to finish the current step.
settings.default_note: atlas default: 450,000 scaled to the context window

settings.title: Where an agent is told to wrap up
settings.what: The context size, in tokens, from which an agent is told to wrap up and write its handoff at its next clean stopping point, for every kind without its own handoff point. At most the hard limit.
settings.cost: Lower hands off sooner: more fresh agents, each cheaper per turn.
settings.basis: Agents told to wrap up from about 285k on a 1M window handed off with room left to finish their current step.
settings.default_note: atlas default: 285,000 scaled to the context window

settings.title: Heavy compiles at once
settings.what: How many queued launches that declare Uses: compile may hold the compile resource at once while agent caps are on. 0 never serializes compiles. Setup's builder cap follows it.
settings.cost: Higher runs more compiles at once: a busier machine, and on a small one memory pressure and resets.
settings.basis: Setup's starter is one slot per 16 hardware threads, at least 1, at most 4: a 16-thread machine gets 1, a 32-thread machine 2. An install that never ran setup gets 1.
settings.default_note: atlas default: 1; setup writes max(1, threads / 16), at most 4

settings.title: GPU runs at once
settings.what: How many queued launches that declare Uses: gpu may hold the gpu resource at once while agent caps are on. 0 never serializes GPU runs.
settings.cost: Higher lets GPU runs overlap, so their timings disturb each other.
settings.basis: gpu is a lock and atlas assigns no device, so a second holder on a two-GPU machine would still land on device 0. Setup writes 1 and probes nothing.

settings.title: Tell the main session when to ask for /compact
settings.what: Past the main session's compact point the PreToolUse hook tells it to ask the user to run /compact (or /clear, once the session restarts high after each compaction), again every 25,000 tokens and more urgently past the hard limit. It is only ever advice: the main session is never blocked, whatever context-mode says.
settings.cost: A line of context at each repeat; the user is asked to compact sooner than they might.
settings.basis: An orchestrator session reached about 735k tokens on 2026-11-14 before anyone asked for a /compact (atlas#9). On by default since it is only advice (ATLAS-CLEAR 0006).

settings.title: Where the main session is told to ask for /compact
settings.what: The context size, in tokens, from which the main session is told to ask the user for /compact, while main-session-compact is on.
settings.cost: Lower compacts sooner: smaller turns, more summaries.
settings.basis: Defaults to the handoff point, so the main session and the agents wrap up at the same size.

settings.title: Ask for a checkpoint before Claude Code compacts on its own
settings.what: atlas predicts where Claude Code will compact the main session on its own (its window, clamped by CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW, less its buffers, and lowered by CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE when set) and, from checkpoint-margin tokens before it, asks the session once to write its checkpoint journal entry. An automatic compaction that comes before the entry is written waits once for it; the checkpoint atlas writes names the entry, or says it is missing.
settings.cost: One line of context a compaction, one journal entry, and at most one deferred compaction a segment (never within a margin of the window's end).
settings.basis: Hooks speak only on a tool call or a prompt, so the request comes a step ahead; Claude Code 2.1.323 skips a proactive automatic compaction a PreCompact hook blocks.

settings.title: How far before the predicted compaction the checkpoint is asked for
settings.what: In tokens. It has to cover one large step, since the request can only come on the next tool call or prompt.
settings.cost: Larger asks earlier, so more work after the checkpoint goes unrecorded in it.
settings.basis: A starting value (ATLAS-CLEAR), to be tuned from the largest per-step context jumps in the logs.

settings.title: When to recommend a clear instead of another compaction
settings.what: The context of the first request after the newest compaction. Past it, the main session's prompts recommend /clear over /compact: atlas writes the session's checkpoint from its own transcript as the clear ends it (SessionEnd), and the cleared session's first hook gives its card (key, rulings, owed work) beside the resume card. 0 never recommends a clear.
settings.cost: A clear drops the summary and whatever was injected again after each compaction; the card and the store carry the state instead.
settings.basis: A long session restarted at 62k, 63k and 69k tokens after its last three compactions, re-injected skill bodies included (ATLAS-CLEAR).
